rich_summary: As the climactic duel between Rama and Ravana continues, the two warriors charge across the battlefield in their chariots, circling and unleashing torrents of arrows like storm clouds. Their charioteers maneuver with dazzling skill while weapons—maces, clubs, axes, and shafts—fill the sky. The violence of the clash shakes the cosmos: seas churn, the earth trembles, the sun dims, and gods, sages, and celestial beings watch anxiously, praying for Rama’s victory. Rama cuts off one of Ravana’s heads, but another instantly grows in its place. Again and again he severs the demon king’s heads—dozens, even hundreds—yet Ravana does not fall. Confounded, Rama reflects that the same arrows that slew many terrible foes now seem powerless against Ravana, hinting that a deeper secret or divine strategy is required to end the battle.

highlight_spans.why: The opening frames the duel as a cosmic spectacle witnessed by all beings and sets the epic scale of the confrontation.
The description of the universe reacting—seas churning, earth shaking, sun dimming—elevates the duel to a mythic, world-shaking event.
Rama beheads Ravana for the first time and the head regrows, revealing the demon king’s terrifying resilience and shifting the stakes of the battle.
Rama’s internal reflection that his legendary arrows now fail against Ravana captures a rare moment of doubt in the hero amid the titanic struggle.

top_scenes.scene_text: Rama and Ravana race across the battlefield in their chariots, circling and firing storms of arrows while the sky fills with weapons.
The cosmic disturbance of the duel—seas churning, mountains trembling, the sun dimmed—while gods and sages watch anxiously from the heavens.
Rama’s arrow slices off one of Ravana’s jeweled heads, which falls to the earth as another head instantly grows from the demon king’s body.
